title: Emergent Matter Research Framework (EMRF): Space-Entropy Compression Across 10 Relativistic and Cosmological Regimes
description: Open-source research framework for the Compressed Space-Time Matter Hypothesis (CSTMH) / Emergent Matter Research Framework (EMRF): spatial ontology X = {x, y, z, d0, d1, ...} with entropy S(X,t) as a state field, and the hypothesis that the galactic acceleration scale is a0 = c H0 / (2 pi). Version note (2026-10-07): an independent audit (docs/SHOW_YOUR_WORK.md) found that earlier releases reported results computed from synthetic data files labelled as observations; those files are now quarantined in data/synthetic/ and those results are withdrawn. The current real-data analysis (SPARC, 153 galaxies, distances and inclinations marginalized) finds the hypothesis a0 = c H0 / (2 pi) neither confirmed nor excluded: gas-dominated galaxies agree with it, the full sample lies 2-4 sigma above it, and the excess comes from galaxies with bulges (5.4 sigma), which no plausible stellar mass-to-light ratio removes (galaxy-specific systematics or a non-universal a0). Bulgeless galaxies prefer a0 ~ 0.93e-10 m/s^2, below c H0 / (2 pi); a0 is systematics-limited at 15-20 percent. The law g = sqrt(g_N^2 + a0 g_N) used in earlier versions is disfavoured by both the galaxy data and Solar System bounds.
